evals.prompt: /interactive-teaching I want to learn enough SQL to answer my own questions about our sales data
evals.expected_output: Classroom initialised, 1-3 mission questions on screen with options and a recommendation, server started, URL reported in one line.
assertions: A .teach/state.json exists in the workspace and assets/teach.css and assets/teach-quiz.js were created
Asks only the two or three questions that most change the first lesson (not a full questionnaire), in the classroom's general thread
The questions probe the concrete goal, current experience and where they will practise
The message reads like a warm teacher getting going, not an onboarding form
A provisional MISSION.md exists with assumptions marked (assumed)
If a starter lesson is drafted, it targets a first win on a made-up but realistic sales table (pass if a starter lesson was reasonably skipped with a stated reason)
The server was started and a 127.0.0.1 URL was obtained, and agent.handled acked
The terminal message tells the learner where the classroom is and how it works, briefly

evals.prompt: /interactive-teaching resume (workspace with one unhandled send: 1/3 quiz, weak recall, a quotes question, Next lesson 'totals per region')
evals.expected_output: Pending send fully handled: recall graded honestly, question answered in the lesson thread, lesson scored 1/3, evidence-based records, next lesson on GROUP BY started with retrieval of the missed quoting items, ack last.
assertions: Lesson 0001 has score 1/3
The recall answer gets feedback grading it partly right and saying WHERE runs before SELECT
The quotes question gets a direct answer (rule, example, what goes wrong)
A new lesson exists (drafting) whose goal is totals per region / GROUP BY
The next lesson's brief asks for diagnostic practice on the missed quoting items (feedback per wrong answer / misconception slugs)
Learning records are atomic: separate records for unquoted text, unquoted dates and WHERE order (not one combined record)
No learning record claims mastery the evidence does not show
Something the learner can use now is made in the same turn (a reference sheet, or a fix to lesson 1's give-away answers or missing explanations)
One overall message on lesson 0001 ties the send together (how it went, focus, what's next)
The terminal recap is short and points to the classroom
agent.handled is 1 and agent.status is waiting at the end

evals.prompt: Write lesson 0002 (GROUP BY + SUM per region for a date range) for the SQL learner
evals.expected_output: One short, cited lesson using the quiz kit, with a recall item and retrieval of lesson-1 weak spots.
assertions: lessons/0002-totals-per-region.html exists and links ../assets/teach.css and ../assets/teach-quiz.js
The lesson states one win near the top
At least one item retrieves a lesson-1 weak spot (quoted string/date literals or WHERE order)
It cites at least one external source with a link and names one primary source
It links back to lesson 0001
Prose is short: under ~900 words, not counting code and quiz items
It uses the real orders table columns in examples
In every .tq-quiz, choices are the same length (longest <= 1.15x shortest in characters)
A warm-up retrieval item on lesson 1 comes before the new material
Quiz items are spread through the lesson: at least two concept sections are each followed by their own check, not all items in one block at the end
It has a 'your turn' production step and a 'try it for real' step outside the page
Wrong multiple-choice options carry data-feedback and data-misconception (diagnostic, not generic)
Practice is scaffolded: at least one tq-fill before writing the query from memory (tq-recall)
There is an explore widget (something to play with) before the learner must demonstrate independently

evals.prompt: /interactive-teaching resume (lesson 2 send repeats the unquoted-text misconception already on record; learner asks for a trick to remember)
evals.expected_output: Teacher recognises the recurring misconception, links it to record 0002, adds the new evidence there (no duplicate record), gives a memorable fix, and makes the next lesson keep retrieving it.
assertions: The reply or round-up tells the learner this is the same quoting slip as lesson 1 (recognises recurrence), not as if it were new
The learner's 'trick to remember' question gets a concrete, memorable rule or mnemonic tied to their own data
learning-records/0002-not-yet-unquoted-text.md gains the new evidence (send 2, filter-west); no duplicate unquoted-text record is created
The unquoted-date record is not marked fixed or superseded (send 2 has no evidence about dates); records stay one misconception each
Lesson 0002 is done and scored 2/3
The next lesson (top customers) is added and its brief asks for retrieval of unquoted-text with targeted feedback
The terminal recap is short (no more than ~6 lines) and points to the classroom
agent.handled is 2 and status waiting

evals.prompt: /interactive-teaching I want to learn beginner yoga to loosen up my stiff lower back, I sit at a desk all day
assertions: Asks only two or three questions, and they include safety (current pain, injuries, medical advice) given the back
A provisional MISSION.md exists with assumptions marked (assumed)
The starter lesson is a guided sequence of real-world steps (poses) with what to notice and how to do each safely, not a reading lesson
The lesson includes clear stop/see-a-professional guidance (sharp pain, numbness, symptoms) and does not overclaim medical benefit
Claims are grounded in cited high-trust sources (health services, clinical guidance, recognised yoga/physio bodies), with one primary source named
Checks fit the topic: recall or multiple choice about cues and safety with targeted feedback; no forced code-style exercise or contrived widget
No database, server or tooling was installed or started to build the lesson (other than the classroom server)
The classroom is set up (server, URL, ack) and the terminal message briefly explains where it is and how it works
The starter lesson passes check-lesson with no errors
The lesson follows the arc: prior knowledge (warm-up, or a baseline question in a first lesson) first, a check after each concept section, and independent application at the end
The lesson ends with the learner producing or performing the objective unaided (a recall/written task or a real-world task with how to tell it worked), not with multiple choice
Any custom widget makes something observable that prose and an exercise could not, and serves the objective (or there is none and none was needed)
check-lesson --render passes: every item renders, responds and reports exactly once, with no script errors

evals.prompt: /interactive-teaching resume (Spanish: lesson 2 send repeats ser-vs-estar in a quiz and a recall; learner asks why location takes estar if the bathroom is always there)
assertions: Tells the learner this is the same ser/estar slip as lesson 1 (recognises recurrence across the quiz and the recall)
Answers 'the bathroom is always there' directly: location takes estar regardless of permanence (with an example)
The recall '¿Dónde es el baño?' gets feedback that it should be está, tied to the same rule
learning-records/0001-not-yet-ser-vs-estar.md gains the new evidence and stays active; no duplicate ser-vs-estar record
Lesson 0002 is done and scored 1/2 (first attempts)
The next lesson (asking for the bill) is added, and its brief has a concrete plan that keeps retrieving ser-vs-estar with expected wrong answers
Lessons 0001 and 0002 keep their existing quiz choices
No database, server or tooling was installed or started to check the Spanish
The terminal recap is short and points to the classroom; agent.handled is 2

Nothing was installed (git itself, servers, tools) beyond the classroom server; the terminal message briefly explains the classroom

The lesson ends with the learner producing or performing the objective unaided (a recall/written task or a real-world task with how to tell it worked), not with multiple choice
Any custom widget makes something observable that prose and an exercise could not, and serves the objective (or there is none and none was needed)
check-lesson --render passes: every item renders, responds and reports exactly once, with no script errors
